new_public_evidence.source: Shaer, Bar, Prinster & Romano (2026), Testing For Distribution Shifts with Conditional Conformal Test Martingales, arXiv:2602.13848v2
new_public_evidence.result: The fixed-reference conditional CTM uses a uniform CDF confidence band such as DKW epsilon=sqrt(log(2/delta)/(2n)); Theorem 3.1 gives conditional anytime type-I <= alpha on the reference-good event; Eq. 12 defines Delta_k as empirical PIT-mean signal minus the confidence penalty; Theorem 3.3 gives power one when Delta_k>0 for small k and, as k->0, an expected-delay rate. The proof gives usable explicit constants: omega >= Delta_0^2/[4(1+Delta_0^2)], t_star=ceil[(16/omega) log(1/(alpha omega))], and E[tau] <= t_star + (32+(4/3)ln 3)/omega + 1.

derived_results.claim: For P=N(0,1), Q=N(mu,r) with r>0 and D_KL(Q||P)>=1, the two fixed score channels s1(x)=x and s2(x)=x^2 satisfy max{|E_Q F_{s1,P}(s1(Y))-1/2|, |E_Q F_{s2,P}(s2(Y))-1/2|} >= 0.163.
derived_results.proof_sketch: By symmetry take mu>=0 and define d=mu/sqrt(1+r). The first signal is a(d)=Phi(d)-1/2. If a>=0.163 we are done. Otherwise Phi(0.421)>0.663 (certified by the alternating lower expansion of exp(-t^2/2) with 1/sqrt(2pi)>0.3989), hence d<0.421. The KL is K(d,r)=0.5[d^2(1+r)+r-1-ln r], increasing in d. For G(r)=K(0.421,r), G is decreasing before its unique minimum and increasing after; conservative log-series bounds give G(0.065)<0.996 and G(3.4)<0.991, so K>=1 forces r<0.065 or r>3.4. Let q(d,r)=P(|Y|>|X|), X~N(0,1). q is increasing in d (folded-normal stochastic ordering) and in r at fixed d: with U=(Y-X)/sqrt(1+r), V=(Y+X)/sqrt(1+r), corr(U,V)=(r-1)/(r+1), q=P(UV>0), and the bivariate-normal lower-orthant term increases with correlation. For r<0.065, q(d,r)<=q(0.421,0.065). Writing q=2(Phi(d)-1/2)+2C with C=P(Y<-|X|), use 2Phi(t)-1<=sqrt(2/pi)t and the Birnbaum Mills lower bound to obtain C<0.0042; also Phi(0.421)<0.6632, hence q<0.3348 and the second signal exceeds 0.1652. For r>3.4, q>=q(0,3.4)=2 arctan(sqrt(3.4))/pi>0.6683, so the second signal exceeds 0.1683. Thus 0.163 is a fully analytic conservative floor; the prior numerical 0.1643729 remains a stronger but non-certified minimax estimate.

derived_results.claim: For the two fixed x/x^2 channels, reference n=684, per-channel DKW delta=0.022 and conditional test alpha=0.003, the r80a floor yields a formal positive effective signal and an explicit conservative expected-stopping bound on the reference-good event.
derived_results.derivation: On each DKW-good event, |E_Q[hat F(score(Y))-1/2]| >= ideal_signal-epsilon and bar_epsilon=epsilon, hence Delta0>=ideal_signal-2epsilon. At least one channel has the ideal floor, so on the intersection of both DKW events the union detector inherits the winning channel's Theorem-3.3 power/delay bound. Reference failure union <=0.044 and conditional alarm union <=0.006, giving unconditional false-alarm <=0.05 by a union bound.
derived_results.scope: Fixed Gaussian alternative; k->0 theorem regime; fixed score maps; expectation bound is conditional on the reference-good event and is intentionally very conservative, not a practical latency prediction.

derived_results.claim: A parameter-free Gaussian alternative avoids estimating the baseline center: combine raw-value rank score s1(x)=x with a second conditional-CTM stream formed from squared non-overlapping pair differences s2(x1,x2)=(x1-x2)^2. For arbitrary Gaussian P and Q with D_KL(Q||P)>=1, the two population PIT-mean signals have a conservative analytic floor >=0.177.
derived_results.proof_sketch: Standardize P conceptually; KL is invariant. The raw-value signal is a(d)=Phi(d)-1/2 with d=|mu|/sqrt(1+r). The non-overlapping difference distribution cancels the mean, so the second signal is v(r)=|2 arctan(sqrt(r))/pi-1/2|. If a<0.177, Phi(0.46)>0.677 implies d<0.46. K(0.46,0.068)<1 and K(0.46,3.25)<1 by conservative log-series bounds, so KL>=1 forces r<0.068 or r>3.25. In the low branch sqrt(r)<0.261 and v is far above 0.177. In the high branch arctan(sqrt(3.25))>1.064 (alternating sin/cos bounds give tan(1.064)<1.8021<sqrt(3.25)); with pi<3.142, 2*1.064/pi>0.67727, hence v>0.17727.
derived_results.benefit: No unknown mean/scale fit is needed; raw rank is affine-invariant and pair differences remove the mean while scale cancels in the ECDF comparison.
derived_results.cost: From 684 baseline observations only 342 disjoint pair scores are iid for ordinary DKW; the live pair channel also advances once per two raw observations. At delta=0.02 its DKW epsilon is about 0.08205, leaving only about 0.01289 after the two-epsilon correction, so its formal delay bound is much looser unless calibration efficiency is improved.
derived_results.status: analytic population floor; finite-reference architecture promising but currently calibration-expensive

negative_or_scope_evidence: The prior 0.1643728991 two-score minimum is still only a numerical estimate; r80 replaces the missing continuum step with a slightly weaker analytic 0.163 theorem rather than overstating the stronger number.

The ~424.6k expected-stop upper bound is a proof-level worst-case certificate from the paper's constants. It should not be interpreted as observed or typical detection delay; practical delay can be orders of magnitude smaller.

The x^2 channel is only generically fixed if the Gaussian baseline center/scale are externally known. Estimating a centering transform from the same reference used for its ECDF would violate the fixed-score calibration argument unless an independent fitting/cross-fitting proof is supplied.

The pair-difference channel repairs unknown-center dependence but halves iid calibration count and test-time clock rate when restricted to disjoint pairs. Using all pairwise differences requires a U-process/U-statistic confidence argument; ordinary DKW cannot be applied to dependent all-pairs scores.

Theorem 3.3's power analysis is for a fixed iid alternative Q and k sufficiently small (with the displayed explicit delay calculation using the k->0 proof). It does not by itself certify transient, drifting, or adversarial post-change sequences.

candidate_new.mechanism: Use an analytically certified portfolio of fixed score channels rather than relying on numerical angular/radial gridding. In the known-standardized Gaussian case, x and x^2 guarantee ideal PIT-mean signal >=0.163 for KL>=1 and therefore admit a direct DKW-to-Delta0-to-delay certificate. For unknown Gaussian center/scale, raw x plus non-overlapping squared pair differences gives a parameter-free ideal floor >=0.177 but needs a more reference-efficient calibration method.
candidate_new.status: known-standardized branch theorem-level; unknown-parameter pair branch promising with finite-reference bottleneck

frontier: Derive a reference-efficient confidence band for the pair-difference score using U-statistic/U-process concentration or a cross-fitted pairing scheme, with a finite-sample anytime CTM proof; target effective calibration substantially above n/2 without pretending dependent all-pairs differences are iid.

Compare the pair-difference route against an independent fit/calibration split for a centered-square score. Quantify fit-error degradation of the 0.163 floor and choose the architecture with the smaller worst-case raw-sample delay under one global false-alarm budget.

If useful, sharpen the analytic 0.163 x/x^2 floor toward the numerical 0.1643729 optimum by solving the low-variance equality point with directed-rounding arithmetic; this is now optional because positivity and a formal delay certificate are already closed.

Run a common-random matched simulation of the early t/F sentinel, the certified x/x^2 conditional-CTM late fallback, and the pair-difference alternative under the same total PFA/error budget across the full Gaussian KL=1 boundary; keep simulation evidence separate from the theorem-level guarantees.

Generalize the score-portfolio principle beyond Gaussian families: select a finite score set before calibration and derive distribution-family-specific lower bounds on max PIT-mean signal rather than relying on one omnibus score.
exact_next_action: Attack the finite-reference bottleneck of the translation-free pair-difference channel: find a primary-source U-empirical-CDF or U-process concentration inequality for all pairwise differences, derive an explicit confidence width for n=684 baseline observations, and check whether the resulting Delta0/delay beats disjoint-pair DKW. If no clean finite-sample band exists, evaluate independent multi-pair cross-fitting with a union/mixture e-process while preserving exact type-I semantics.
